![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/cd19503a1b72cd353cd2bacad0c187a1f83881d511b6ffcf0e99755ab9f682a9.png)

A plate with mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves $y={x}^{3}$ and $y=x$, as shown above. Given that the region has an area of $\frac{1}{4},$ find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=1.$
worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,{x}^{3}\le y\le x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/4463119c9f2ff0c1c658dd573add51a000cc50187e7dd59f39a40ba7c3abfce2.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=4M.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{x}|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{x}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-1)^{2}[y]_{y={x}^{3}}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-2x+1)(x-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{\int }_{0}^{1}x-2{x}^{2}+2{x}^{4}-{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4M{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{2{x}^{5}}{5}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4M(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{5}-\frac{1}{6}-0) \\  & =\frac{4M}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
